title: Inductive Deductive Synthesis: Co-Evolving Code-and-Proof Generation
claim: Two coupled synthesis steps each feed the other, so code and proof improve together incrementally under checker feedback.
layout: 2 boxes left and right, curved arrows forming a cycle, checker in center
description: A small cyclic diagram on a white background. A blue rounded box on the left, titled 'Synthesize Code' with a code-bracket icon, says 'writes/refines impl' and contains a snippet with 'def inc (s)' and 'def read (s)'. A green rounded box on the right, titled 'Synthesize Proof' with a green checkmark icon, says 'proves code property' and contains 'Lemm. rd_af_inc: admit.'. A blue arrow curves along the top from code to proof, labeled 'Code gives the structure to prove'. A green arrow curves along the bottom from proof back to code, labeled 'Proof reveals unsatisfied parts in code'. A pink box with a black shield icon, labeled 'Proof Assistant', sits in the center. The eye goes first to the two large colored titles, then follows the loop.
caption: Code and proof advance jointly and incrementally with IDS; the proof assistant grades each partial step.
abstract: AI agents increasingly excel at generating, testing, and refining code. However, they fall short on tasks requiring formal guarantees of full coverage that testing alone cannot provide. Distributed systems are a prime example: properties such as consistency between reads and writes must hold under every possible interleaving of events. Mechanized formal verification can guarantee such correctness, but typically demands months to years of expert effort. As evidence, even SOTA coding agents (Codex with GPT-5.4 and Claude Code with Opus 4.6) succeed on only 2/7 distributed key-value-store specifications. In this paper, we present the first effective approach to addressing this gap, Inductive Deductive Synthesis (IDS), which incrementally co-evolves implementation and proof, and learns from failed attempts to systematically try promising strategies. Built as an agentic LLM system, IDS achieves 7/7 in about 6.9 hours and $106 per spec on average, roughly 200× faster than expert effort and 17% cheaper than SOTA agents. IDS further incorporates performance feedback into the same loop, yielding implementations up to 3× faster than published verified systems.
